Mound Christmas Tree lights switch-on 2026: Norwegian roots and Edinburgh’s best indie markets

November 16, 2026 by Andrew Girdwood Leave a Comment

Edinburgh’s civic Christmas season officially began on Monday, 16 November 2026, when Lord Provost Robert Aldridge joined representatives from Vestland and the Norwegian Consulate to switch on the Mound Christmas tree lights at 6.30 pm. Following a 5.50 pm procession from the City Chambers led by the Candlemakers, the half-hour ceremony in the Assembly Hall Courtyard blended Scottish civic pageantry with a forty-year diplomatic tradition.

What happened on the Mound between 6.00 pm and 6.30 pm

At 5.50 pm, the Candlemakers led the civic party out of the City Chambers on the High Street, arriving at the Assembly Hall Courtyard on Mound Place at 6.00 pm. Steeped in stone and flanked by New College’s Gothic towers, the courtyard provided an intimate acoustic pocket sheltered from the evening chill sweeping up from Waverley Valley.

Piper Louise Marshall opened the gathering with traditional Highland bagpipe music before Gilmerton Primary School choir sang two Christmas carols by lantern light. Short speeches followed from Lord Provost Robert Aldridge alongside delegates from Vestland County and the Norwegian Consulate. At 6.30 pm, the party threw the switch to illuminate the tree overlooking Princes Street, with Louise Marshall playing again as the lights came up against the dark Old Town skyline.

The Norwegian connection: Why Vestland gifts the Mound tree

While visitors often assume the Mound tree is simply another city decoration, the 18-metre fir carries specific wartime weight. Since 1986, the western Norwegian county of Vestland (formerly Hordaland) has gifted the Christmas tree to Edinburgh each year to express gratitude for Scotland’s support during the Second World War.

During the German occupation of Norway between 1940 and 1945, Scotland served as a vital base and safe haven for exiled Norwegian forces, merchant sailors, and civilians. Scottish ports hosted the Shetland Bus operations and Norwegian naval units, forging a bond that outlasted the war. Although the tree has been sourced locally from Scottish forests since 2008 to avoid transporting timber across the North Sea and reduce carbon emissions, Vestland and the Norwegian Honorary Consulate General still present it formally as a fixture of Edinburgh’s winter calendar.

Beyond the Mound: Where to find Edinburgh’s indie Christmas Markets

Standing at the foot of the Mound gives you a clear view of the glowing Norwegian fir, and the immediate bottleneck of East Princes Street Gardens next door. Central Edinburgh is undeniably atmospheric in November and December, particularly when dusk settles before 4.00 pm, yet the main commercial market between Waverley Bridge and the Scott Monument quickly becomes shoulder-to-shoulder.

Once you have admired the Mound tree and walked the cobbles of the Old Town, step away from the main tourist thoroughfare. Independent makers, neighbourhood arts hubs, and community markets across the capital offer locally crafted gifts, hot street food, and room to breathe.

  • Castle Street Christmas Market (New Town): Just a five-minute walk north of the Mound, this LocalMotive-run market sets up directly beneath the Castle rock on select dates between 25 November and 22 December 2026, focusing on small-batch Scottish food, jewellery, and knitwear.
  • Summerhall Winter Market (Newington): Taking over the former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College on 5 and 6 December 2026 (11.00 am–5.00 pm), Summerhall’s sprawling courtyard and halls host over 60 independent artists, ceramicists, and local drink producers.
  • Edinburgh Printmakers Christmas Market (Fountainbridge): Hosted at Castlemills on Dundee Street across 28 and 29 November 2026, this market pairs original fine-art prints and textiles with festive menus from Café KUBA.
  • 3D2D Christmas Art, Craft & Design Fair (George Street): Returning to the 200-year-old Assembly Rooms on 5 and 6 December 2026, this indoor fair brings together more than 100 juried Scottish artists and designers under one roof.
  • Christmas Community Makers Market (Leith): Held aboard the Vine Trust barge at Prince of Wales Dock off Ocean Drive on 21 November 2026, offering waterfront browsing alongside local makers and warm refreshments.
  • Bethany Christian Trust Christmas Market (Leith): Running on 4 and 5 December 2026, combining handmade crafts with sustainable Grade A Nordmann Fir Christmas trees sold to fund homelessness support across Scotland.
  • Stockbridge and Grassmarket Weekly Markets: Every Saturday in the Grassmarket (10.00 am–5.00 pm) and every Sunday on Saunders Street in Stockbridge (10.00 am–4.00 pm), Edinburgh’s regular neighbourhood markets pivot toward seasonal hampers, smoked salmon, artisan bakes, and small-batch gifts.
